## Why This Is Asked

This question tests cost-aware design for SAP on AWS, balancing licensing, performance, and scalability in a real-world, beginner-friendly way.

## Key Concepts

- Reserved Instances / Savings Plans
- Spot Instances
- Auto Scaling Groups
- Resource tagging for cost allocation
- AWS Budgets alerts

```yaml
# Minimal CloudFormation snippet
BudgetAlarmRole:
  Type: AWS::IAM::Role
  Properties:
    AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
      Version: '2012-10-17'
      Statement:
        - Effect: Allow
          Principal:
            Service: budgets.amazonaws.com
          Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
    Path: '/'
    Policies:
      - PolicyName: BudgetTagPolicy
        PolicyDocument:
          Version: '2012-10-17'
          Statement:
            - Effect: Allow
              Action: ['tag:GetResources','tag:TagResources']
              Resource: '*'
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- SAP HANA System Replication
- Route 53 failover routing
- AWS Backup PITR and cross-region backups
- IAM per-region roles and cross-account trust
- Step Functions, CloudWatch alarms, and SSM

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  DRRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: 'arn:aws:iam::SRC_ACCOUNT:root'
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DRAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'ec2:DescribeInstances'
                  - 'route53:*'
                  - 'backup:*'
                Resource: '*'
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a robust, automated cross‑region DR solution for SAP on AWS with concrete RPO/RTO targets, DNS failover, and immutable backups.

## Key Concepts

- SAP HANA System Replication (ASYNC) across regions
- Route 53 failover routing and health checks
- Immutable backups in S3 (Object Lock) and cross-region retention
- CloudFormation/IaC for cross-region roles and DNS records
- Cutover automation and rollback considerations

## Code Example

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  CrossRegionDRRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: SAPCrossRegionDRRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DRAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:PutObject
                  - s3:GetObject
                Resource: '*'
```

```yaml
DRRecordPrimary:
  Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
  Properties:
    HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZoneId
    Name: sap-hana.example.com
    Type: A
    SetIdentifier: Primary
    Failover: PRIMARY
    TTL: 60
    ResourceRecords:
      - !Ref PrimaryIP

DRRecordSecondary:
  Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
  Properties:
    HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZoneId
    Name: sap-hana.example.com
    Type: A
    SetIdentifier: Secondary
    Failover: SECONDARY
    TTL: 60
    ResourceRecords:
      - !Ref SecondaryIP
```

- How would you validate the DR failover path under simulated outages?
- What metrics and alarms ensure RPO/RTO remain within targets?

## Why This Is Asked

- Cross-region blue/green deployment

```yaml
# Minimal cross-region IAM role (CloudFormation)
Resources:
  CrossRegionSAPRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:aws:iam::${SourceAccount}:root'
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPPatchPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ec2:StartInstances
                  - ec2:StopInstances
                  - ec2:DescribeInstances
                  - ssm:SendCommand
                  - route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets
                  - route53:GetHealthCheckStatus
                Resource: '*'
```

```yaml
# Minimal IaC: Trusting role for canary upgrades
Resources:
  CanaryRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: "arn:aws:iam::<TEST_ACCOUNT_ID>:root"
            Action: "sts:AssumeRole"
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: CanaryPolicy
          PolicyDocument:

                  - ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation
                  - ec2:DescribeInstances
                Resource: "*"
```

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  SSMPatchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ssm.amazonaws.com
```

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  SAPRemediationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Path: '/'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPRemediation
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:SendCommand
                Resource: '*'
  SAPRemediationFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt SAPRemediationRole.Arn
      Runtime: nodejs14.x
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          const AWS = require('aws-sdk');
          exports.handler = async () => { console.log('Restart SAP HANA if needed'); };
  SAPHANA_CPU_Alarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: SAPHANA_CPU_Alarm
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/EC2
      Dimensions:
        - Name: InstanceId
          Value: !Ref SAPInstance
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 80
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !GetAtt SAPRemediationFunction.Arn
```
